blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, what does Java's single-inheritance rule mean for a class that needs behaviour from several sources?

options.text: It can extend just one class, but it can hold any number of composed objects
options.says: The page says a class can compose multiple behaviors but can only extend one class.

options.text: It can extend several classes, provided that each of them is declared abstract
options.says: The page says Java has single inheritance, so a class extends only one class, abstract or not.

options.text: It can hold just one composed object, but it can extend any number of classes
options.says: The page says the opposite: composition has no such limitation, and a class extends only one class.

questions.stem: Per this page, why do records push a design towards composition?

options.text: They are implicitly final, so no class can extend them
options.says: The page says records are implicitly final and cannot be extended.

options.text: They are implicitly abstract, so each use must extend them
options.says: The page says records are implicitly final and cannot be extended, so no use extends them.

options.text: They are implicitly sealed, so only listed classes extend them
options.says: The page says records are implicitly final and cannot be extended at all.

concepts: Records are implicitly final and cannot be extended, so they lead a design towards composition.
Java lets a class extend only one class, so combining behaviour from several sources needs composition.
